findings: Solved 2026-10-29 on the owner's request (Physics XI pending exercises into Practice, as for Computer Science): the Chapter 5 exercise (PDF 116-118, printed 113-115) with every printed question answered in English and Roman Urdu: 12 MCQs (keyed checkpoints), 11 short answer, 6 constructed response and 9 comprehensive questions (self-checks with model answers; comparisons as answer tables) and 8 numerical problems (worked line by line). Drafts for the academic review.

The book prints no MCQ key; keys worked out from the chapter: 1a 2d 3a 4b 5b 6a 7c 8c 9d 10c 11d 12a. MCQ 5.6: (a) chosen (Stokes' law in the chapter). MCQ 5.4: (b) Bernoulli's effect chosen (the chapter's horizontal-pipe result); a Venturi-effect key is also defensible.

Numerical 5.3: the exponents of the printed area and of the printed stress answer cannot be read with certainty in the scan, so the printed 0.00455 is not boxed (not verifiable); worked with the area as read (1 × 10⁻⁴ m²) and copper Y = 1.1 × 10¹¹ N m⁻² from Table 5.1 (sweep 2026-11-13).
Numerical 5.6: Bernoulli gives 14.37 m s⁻¹ (≈ 14.4); the book prints 14.3 m s⁻¹, and the question itself already states the exit speed as 14 m s⁻¹. Noted in the answer, no correction box.

Numerical 5.8: the printed 9.90 m s⁻¹ does not follow from Stokes' law with the chapter's own values (ρ = 1000 kg m⁻³, η(air) = 0.019 × 10⁻³ N s m⁻² from the table in 5.13): ≈ 28.7 m s⁻¹. Book correction box (verified 2026-11-13).

Comprehensive 5.8 is printed 'practical equations of Bernoulli's equation'; answered with the practical applications of Section 5.12. 5.4 and 5.6 both ask for the continuity derivation (answered from the mass-conservation and statement angles respectively).

Answers beyond the chapter (labelled): short 5.8 (Archimedes and the crown), CRQ 5.2 (adhesion vs cohesion), part of CRQ 5.6 (quantum effects), the real-raindrop note in numerical 5.8; MCQ 5.11 (Venturi mask) is answered from Bernoulli's principle.
